propositions: rebar sign-review deterministically fails with store-read-failure on a PASS plan when any untracked file exists in the shared tracker, so a paid LLM review is discarded and the claim/close gate stays blocked.
Root cause: resign.py:146 calls generation.collect without ignore_untracked, defaulting to strict git status --porcelain that includes untracked files, unlike the intended --untracked-files=no.

The failure is content- and name-agnostic (purely the git-status check), refuting a partial-JSON parse hypothesis; tracked dirty state still fails under both settings so the real guarantee is preserved.
This is a missed site of already-fixed bug class d7cb-22ae, whose fix touched __init__.py and generation.py but never resign.py, orchestrator.py, or attest.py.
orchestrator.py:650 silently swallows the same error and forces an expensive full multi-pass LLM re-review instead of the cheap drift-refresh probe, a money/latency defect with no visible error.
Fix passes ignore_untracked=True at the four read sites that fingerprint the committed head, with regression tests asserting tolerance of unrelated untracked files while blocking tracked-dirty state.
